title: Prioritize and Execute
coreMove: pause long enough to choose the controlling problem, act on it hard, then look up and choose again
sourcePressure: Leaders restore order in chaos by detaching, identifying the highest-priority problem, executing it, then reassessing.
sourceAnchorsNote: source contains no named anecdote for this chapter

counterintuition: leadership is harder than it looks
tryThisNow: ask yourself how to be a better leader

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: prevents the timestamp+named-protagonist template from dominating the chapter

exampleSpecs.domain: aquarium life-support pump failure before opening
exampleSpecs.audience: an aquarium operations manager with alarms from three tanks at once
exampleSpecs.stakes: animals and visitors are both at risk if the team scatters
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the manager steps back from the alarm panel, identifies oxygen in the reef tank as first priority, assigns one technician, then delays visitor messaging until life support stabilizes
exampleSpecs.firstImage: an oxygen meter flashes low beside a darkened reef tank window

exampleSpecs.domain: alpine rescue after an avalanche beacon signal splits
exampleSpecs.audience: a rescue lead with weather worsening and two possible search zones
exampleSpecs.stakes: searchers can waste minutes chasing every clue
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the lead takes one breath, chooses the strongest beacon line, sends one probe team, and keeps a second team staged until the first result returns
exampleSpecs.firstImage: You are close enough to see this: beacon screen blinks two arrows above a field of broken snow.

exampleSpecs.domain: food truck festival power outage at noon
exampleSpecs.audience: a festival operations lead with vendors, guests, and health inspectors calling at once
exampleSpecs.stakes: food safety fails if power restoration competes with crowd appeasement
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the lead first gets cold storage onto the backup circuit, then posts one guest update, then checks vendor cooking lines in order
exampleSpecs.firstImage: The first thing you register is physical: breaker panel hangs open while a freezer alarm chirps behind the taco truck.

exampleSpecs.domain: newsroom election night results system glitch
exampleSpecs.audience: a managing editor with reporters demanding fixes for every race page
exampleSpecs.stakes: a wrong call can publish if the team works every symptom at once
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the editor freezes publication for unverified races, assigns one data editor to the source feed, and only then lets page producers fix display errors
exampleSpecs.firstImage: "Hold there," someone says. Precinct dashboard freezes at 68 percent counted under the studio lights.

exampleSpecs.domain: dental office sterilizer failure before a full morning schedule
exampleSpecs.audience: a practice manager juggling patients, hygienists, and instruments
exampleSpecs.stakes: infection-control priority must outrank keeping the schedule intact
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the manager cancels the first elective block, routes critical instruments to a partner clinic, and tells the front desk the exact patient sentence to use
exampleSpecs.firstImage: Later, the team will trace the lesson back to this: autoclave tray sits cool with a failed cycle strip beside it.

exampleSpecs.domain: manufacturing plant chemical spill alarm during shift change
exampleSpecs.audience: a plant supervisor with evacuation, containment, and staffing questions colliding
exampleSpecs.stakes: people can move into danger if the first priority is wrong
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the supervisor chooses personnel accountability first, assigns containment to the trained crew only, then updates production after the headcount closes
exampleSpecs.firstImage: What changes once this is in front of everyone: yellow absorbent sock lies half-unrolled beside the spill threshold?

skillTargets: choose the controlling priority under simultaneous alarms
use detachment and reassessment as a sequence
distinguish prioritization from tunnel vision or speed alone

tryThisNowSpec: List the three active problems in front of you, circle the one that controls the others, and write the first action that moves only that problem.
